pr_comments: Hi, @turbaszek can I ask for review?

@turbaszek @feluelle @ephraimbuddy 
I have doubts whether we should allow third-party systems to create and update, delete entries. I don't think this is expected because we store metadata from the execution of a specific task there.  We don't want other systems to be able to affect task execution.  For customizable configuration, we have variables. The user will be able to delete XCOM entries by cleaning the task instance. WDYT?

@mik-laj I understand you point.

Hm.. I could imagine having multiple airflow instances which might want to share those xcom values with each other. WDYT?

@feluelle  These API will not address this problem. I want to build an API for third systems, not an internal API.  In my opinion, API for third-party systems should maintain backward compatibility and should provide access to the most important operations. Building an API that is too rich in features or provides too much information causes problems with maintaining backward compatibility.

I would not want this API to be only access to the database via HTTP, but it was an API that will easily allow you to build new applications on it, e.g. applications for monitoring multiple instances of Airflow and provide mult-tenant view.

> I have doubts whether we should allow third-party systems to create and update, delete entries. I don't think this is expected because **we store metadata** from the execution of a specific task there. We don't want other systems to be able to **affect task execution**. For customizable configuration, we have variables.

I agree here. I think that users should not be able to update XCom, TaskInstance and other "task execution-related" entities. 


> Hm.. I could imagine having multiple airflow instances which might want to share those xcom values with each other. WDYT?

I think in this case read only access should be enough.
We should allow setting TaskInstance state as we do allow that in the Webserver

> We should allow setting TaskInstance state as we do allow that in the Webserver

True, I forgot about this. But still, this is very limited update option.

issue_context.title: API Endpoint - CRUD - XCOM
issue_context.body:
Hello 

We need to create several endpoints that perform basic CRUD operations on **XCOM Entries*. We need the following endpoints:

POST /dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{dag_run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id}/xcomEntries
DELETE /dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{dag_run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id}/xcomEntries/{xcom_key}
PATCH /dags/{dag_id}/dagRuns/{dag_run_id}/taskInstances/{task_id}/xcomEntries/{xcom_key}

It depends on https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/8134

Detailed information is available in the issue:
https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/8118

LOVE,
comments: Hi, @mik-laj , I know the log_endpoint is not merged yet but should I start working on this?
Yes. You can work on other tickets if you are blocked.

review_comments:
```suggestion
    if session.query(XCom).filter(XCom.dag_id == dag_id,
                                       XCom.task_id == task_id,
                                       XCom.key == xcom_key).delete() == 0:
    
```

You could do something like this to make the code shorter, delete returns the number of rows deleted

Yeah. The suggestion is good especially when the query is not long. Here, the query is long and according to the Zen of python, Readability counts, that's why I assigned the number of rows deleted to entry and check it in the next line.
I think this may result in error if there's no `field` attribute of `xcom_entry`.

Commit is performed by `@provide_session` and I'm wondering if we need another one here explicit. I think using the one from `provide_session` has the advantage that if returning response will fail then there will be no change on db level. WDYT? @mik-laj @feluelle @potiuk

> [...] then there will be no change on db level.

Which is correct. So I am for removing the manual commit from there.
